messages:
Aisha (Lumen): Hey CS, during our onboarding smoke tests we see a flurry of 401s followed by 429s. Happens only when we run the suite in our k8s job parallelized across 25 pods.
Priya (CS): thanks for the report. Quick question: are you using ephemeral tokens (short TTL) or a long-lived key in CI? Any HTTP sidecars or auth proxies in the pod?
Aisha (Lumen): ephemeral via our token service, rotating every 45s. We also have an envoy sidecar that adds tracing and does outbound TLS.
Alex (Eng): can you paste a couple of request/response headers from the proxy logs around the 401s? Looking for Authorization, x-request-id, and any cache-related headers.
Aisha (Lumen): snippet from envoy log:
```
-> POST /v1/generate 401
request_headers: {
  "authorization": "Bearer eyJ...oldtoken",
  "x-forwarded-for": "10.0.3.12",
  "x-request-id": "req-9a12"
}
response_headers: { "www-authenticate": "Bearer realm=\"redwood\"" }

-> retry same call -> 429
request_headers: {
  "authorization": "Bearer eyJ...newtoken",
  "x-request-id": "req-9a13"
}
response_headers: { "x-rate-limit-remaining": "0", "x-rate-limit-reset": "2323457100" }
```
Priya (CS): interesting sequence: initial 401 using an expired token, then a retry with a fresh token that hits a burst limit and returns 429. Do your pods share a token-cache via the sidecar? Envoy might be caching the Authorization header or reusing a connection that was authorized with the old token.
Nitin (SRE): adding: our gateway attributes rate buckets per-token *and* per-source IP depending on the policy. If many pods all refresh and hit with the new token at the same instant, you can blow the per-token and per-source buckets. Also, if retries are aggressive, that amplifies the effect.
Alex (Eng): immediate mitigations to try without infra changes: a) make SDK token provider do a proactive fetch with jitter, b) enable single-flight token refresh so only one pod refreshes at a time per host, c) add small randomized retry/backoff. For Python SDK try config:
```
Redwood.configure(token_provider=lazy_rotation_provider,
                  max_concurrency=4,
                  token_refresh={"mode":"singleflight","jitter_ms":300},
                  retry_policy={"max_retries":2,"base_ms":200})
```
Alex (Eng): also, if your CI can use a longer-lived CI key during the parallel ramp that avoids rotation, that isolates whether the rotation timing is root cause.
Aisha (Lumen): we can try the longer-lived key as a test. But long-term we want to keep rotation in prod. Our concern is Envoy caching; is there a header we can set to prevent caching of Authorization in the sidecar?
Nitin (SRE): envoy respects Vary and cache-control only when explicitly configured. If it has an HTTP caching filter or a lua script that manipulates headers it could be copying or holding Authorization. Ask your infra team to ensure the sidecar does not store or rewrite Authorization, and to preserve Connection: keep-alive so TLS sessions are reused.
Priya (CS): temporary playbook for your onboarding: 1) run one test matrix with the long-lived key to confirm token rotation is the culprit, 2) if confirmed, apply SDK single-flight token refresh + low concurrency + jitter during ramp, 3) update sidecar config to not cache Authorization and increase keepalive idle (or bypass sidecar for CI). We'll document this in your account notes.
Aisha (Lumen): ok starting a canary run with a CI key now. Will also ping infra about Envoy lua hooks.
(12 minutes)
Aisha (Lumen): canary with long-lived key = no 401s, no 429s. Looks clean.
Priya (CS): that strongly suggests rotation timing + sidecar behavior is the root cause. We'll mark the account as "needs sidecar auth pass-through" in onboarding and put a renewal risk note: if they keep a slow-sidecar setup, production ramp could see rate/backoff incidents.
Alex (Eng): engineering follow-up: we'll add a telemetry tag in the SDK to detect high token refresh churn and surface a banner in the console for customers running short-lived tokens behind proxies. Filing ENG ticket now.
deploy-bot: rolling out redwood-py@v2.1.4 with singleflight token refresh patch (canary)
Aisha (Lumen): thanks everyone. We'll coordinate infra changes and then switch back to ephemeral tokens. I'll update this thread when Envoy config is merged.
